projects.name: Timewizer
projects.description: Standalone desktop app for building school timetables, with teacher substitutions, cover sheets, undo/redo and Excel/CSV export.

projects.name: Orbit
projects.description: Connect, browse, back up and mount your cloud storage with wizards and plain-language screens. Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox, S3, SFTP and network shares.

projects.name: Stingray
projects.tagline: Your folders, cloud drives and servers in one window.
projects.description: A clean, modern file manager with Google Drive, OneDrive and Dropbox built in, plus SMB, SFTP and NFS network drives. Tabs and split view, archive browsing, undo/redo, a built-in terminal and a preview panel.

projects.name: Burn It!
projects.tagline: Make bootable USB drives from any ISO.
projects.description: Writes Linux and Windows ISOs to USB from either operating system. Built with Tauri (Rust + web UI).

projects.name: Graphite Mail
projects.tagline: Offline mail and calendar for Linux.
projects.description: A native Linux client for Microsoft 365 mail and calendar via Microsoft Graph.

projects.name: Madrasa
projects.description: Offline-capable school administration: students, attendance, exams, fees and finance, teachers, reports and backups, plus transport, hostel and inventory with directory login, and an early Nexus hub for joining several schools. Alpha, for testers only.

projects.name: Rabita
projects.tagline: Join Linux to your domain, the friendly way.
projects.description: A setup wizard that joins Linux desktops to an Active Directory domain: work login, network drives and printers. In early development, no release yet.

projects.name: Lobster Browser
projects.description: Built on Firefox ESR with ad and tracker blocking, privacy defaults and a calm new-tab page. A private built-in AI agent is planned. First preview, Linux only.

projects.name: SkyPop
projects.description: A Pang-inspired arcade game written in Rust with macroquad: ten stages, power-ups and a boss fight.

projects.name: Teamux
projects.tagline: Microsoft Teams, made to work on Linux.
projects.description: An unofficial Microsoft Teams desktop client for Linux with native Wayland, PipeWire screen sharing and camera support. Early preview; not affiliated with Microsoft.
